assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, the active peptide forms, and their pharmacological exploitation) has produced a therapeutic class that has changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and shown cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality sits in defining the physiological hormone and its actions; impact is large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Basic physiology and peptide identification are best captured by Drucker, Holst and Mojsov; Knudsen is the key figure for the long-acting drug development and could displace one name if translation is emphasised. Other early contributors (for example Habener) are not on the supplied credit list, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and large randomised outcome trials; widely adopted and clearly timely.
uncertainties: Who among the many contributors should be credited, and whether basic physiology and drug development should be recognised together, is unresolved.
My recollection of the credit history is from general knowledge and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method for causal control of defined cell populations with light; the discovery of channelrhodopsins and their transfer into neurons is original, and the method is now used throughout biology.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenboeck's earlier genetic light-control work) are interwoven, and six names exceed the three-person limit. I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel as a plausible split between tool discovery and use.
assessment.maturity: Method is mature and independently validated in thousands of studies; clinical use is emerging (vision restoration) but not required for recognition.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the tool discoverers and the neuronal implementers are disputed.
Ernst Bamberg, Edward Boyden and Gero Miesenboeck would be omitted under any three-person choice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; this is a new therapeutic modality with clear conceptual originality and patient impact, and it is extending to autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed costimulatory CAR designs and clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Others (Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner, Gross) are outside the supplied credit list, so a fair configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, multiple independent clinical datasets and long-term follow-up; still-evolving toxicity and solid-tumour limits but timely.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit (not on the list) may complicate attribution.
Long-term durability and safety data continue to accrue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that chaperonins actively assist protein folding in cells, overturning the view that folding is spontaneous, with consequences for protein-misfolding disease and cell physiology. A clean, original and foundational discovery.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl are the two clearly decisive contributors with a clean pairing; the supplied credit supports a fair two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Established for decades, replicated and in textbooks; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Medical rather than purely chemical or biological framing may be debated.
Other contributors to chaperone biology are not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined an intracellular signalling pathway from ER to nucleus, with consequences for secretory physiology, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease, and cancer. Originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori led discovery of Ire1 signalling and the Hac1/XBP1 axis; the pairing is natural. Other contributors such as Ron or Harding are not on the supplied credit list, and I cannot assess that omission fully.
assessment.maturity: Mature, broadly confirmed and still productive; timing appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether the PERK/ATF6 arms and their discoverers should be recognised alongside is unresolved.
Direct therapeutic validation is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective BCR-ABL inhibition turned chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable disease and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Impact on patients and on the field is very large.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation drugs) form a plausible trio; Rowley/Nowell and Witte/Baltimore groundwork was credited elsewhere and is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature with long-term survival data and independent replication; recognition is timely to overdue.
uncertainties: Preceding Nobel-level work on BCR-ABL biology complicates how much of the chain remains to credit.
The relative weight of drug discovery versus clinical translation is a judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrated that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis, establishing cytokine blockade as a paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease and enabling biologic therapies across several diseases.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini form a coherent pair for the concept and clinical proof. Contributions from the anti-TNF antibody developers and others are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed over 25 years with broad clinical use; timely or overdue.
uncertainties: I am not certain that both named individuals are living and eligible; this should be checked.
As a rheumatology specialist I note the risk of over-weighting my own field and have tried to apply the common criteria.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general, scalable culture system for human tissue biology, disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine, building on Lgr5 stem-cell identification.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader; Sato was the first author of the key intestinal organoid work. The pairing is straightforward on the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and replicated; clinical translation is early, so some may judge it slightly premature relative to others on my ballot.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is still largely prospective.
Other organoid pioneers (for example work from pluripotent-cell approaches) could complicate credit.
